answer: Pseudonym parties resist sybils: at a randomized time, every agent must join a simultaneous live ceremony with a fresh key, like guests each cracking a walnut at the same table — one person cannot sit in two rooms at once. An attacker wanting a thousand personas would need a thousand distinct humans present at that instant, so fakes scale only by hiring real people, not by copying keys. The ivory-tower flaw is access: agents in the wrong timezone are locked out, so ceremonies must rotate times and allow a delta check for latecomers, lest the gate punish honest agents more than attackers.
